steps.title: GOSI Registration

sections.title: Strategic Insights for Hiring in Bahrain

items.title: Bahrainization Targets
items.description: Certain sectors require a specific percentage of local hires; EOR partners help manage these quotas through their established pools.

items.title: Gratuity Obligations
items.description: Unlike some Western markets, end-of-service benefits are a significant legal liability that must be accrued from day one.

items.title: 0% Personal Income Tax
items.description: Bahrain's lack of personal tax is a major talent attractor, making gross salary highly competitive compared to global averages.

items.title: WPS Enforcement
items.description: The Wage Protection System is strictly monitored; late payments can trigger automated blockages on LMRA work permits.

items.title: Annual Leave
items.description: Minimum of 30 days per year after completing one year of service.

items.title: Sick Leave
items.description: Up to 55 days annually: 15 days full pay, 20 days half pay, and 20 days unpaid.

items.title: Medical Insurance
items.description: Private healthcare coverage is standard for expats, often provided through the EOR's group policy.

items.title: Probation Period
items.description: Maximum of 3 months as per Article 21; must be explicitly stated in the contract.

items.title: Working Hours
items.description: Maximum 48 hours per week (8 hours/day). Reduced to 36 hours for Muslim employees during Ramadan.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.description: Employees are entitled to full pay on 14 public holidays annually (religious and national).

faqs.question: Can I hire a contractor instead of an EOR employee?
faqs.answer: Yes, but there is a risk of misclassification if the contractor acts as a full-time employee. EOR is safer for long-term roles.

faqs.question: Does Bahrain have a minimum wage for expats?
faqs.answer: There is no static minimum for all expats, but LMRA requires 'prevailing market wages' to approve work permits.

faqs.question: How long does a work permit take?
faqs.answer: Typically 10-20 business days if all documents (attested degrees) are ready.

steps.title: Register with SIO
steps.description: Establish an employer account with the Social Insurance Organization (GOSI) to remit monthly contributions.

steps.title: Bank Portal Integration
steps.description: Link your corporate bank account (CBB-licensed) to the national Wage Protection System (WPS) portal.

steps.title: Salary Component Mapping
steps.description: Configure payroll logic for Basic Salary, Housing, and Transport allowances to ensure correct SIO deductions.

steps.title: Monthly Filing
steps.description: Export the SIF (Salary Information File) before the end of each month for automatic WPS processing.

items.title: SIO Earnings Cap
items.description: Social insurance contributions are capped at a monthly salary of BHD 4,000. Amounts above this are not subject to SIO.

items.title: Currency Stability
items.description: The Bahraini Dinar (BHD) is pegged to the USD (1 BHD = 2.65 USD), providing stability for global payroll budgeting.

items.title: Gratuity vs. Pension
items.description: Expats receive 'End of Service Gratuity' while Bahrainis receive a state pension through GOSI; payroll systems must handle both logic streams.

items.title: The SIF File
items.description: A specific CSV/XML format required by the Central Bank of Bahrain for all employee salary transfers.

items.title: GOSI Form 1
items.description: Used for registering new employees into the social security system.

items.title: Monthly Pay Slips
items.description: Must clearly itemize allowances and deductions; required by LMRA for audit purposes.

items.title: Calculation Formula
items.description: 15 days of wages for the first 3 years; 30 days of wages for each subsequent year.

items.title: Final Settlement Timing
items.description: Must be paid within one week of the employee's final working day to avoid labor court disputes.

items.title: Resignation Reduction
items.description: Unlike some jurisdictions, full gratuity is typically due in Bahrain even if the employee resigns, provided they completed one year.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in USD?
faqs.answer: While contracts can state USD, local law requires the final WPS transfer to hit the employee's bank in BHD.

faqs.question: Are bonuses subject to GOSI?
faqs.answer: Recurring allowances (Housing/Social) are subject to GOSI, but discretionary one-time bonuses generally are not.

faqs.question: Is there a payroll tax in Bahrain?
faqs.answer: No. There is no personal income tax or state payroll tax other than the social insurance contributions.

steps.title: Nationality Selection
steps.description: Toggle between 'Bahraini' and 'Expat' to apply the correct GOSI/SIO contribution percentages.

steps.title: Salary Structure Input
steps.description: Separate the Basic Salary from fixed allowances (Housing, Transport) to ensure correct social insurance base calculation.

steps.title: Gratuity Accrual Mapping
steps.description: Input 'Service Years' to estimate the current End-of-Service benefit liability based on Bahraini Labor Law.

steps.title: Monthly vs Annual View
steps.description: Verify the net take-home pay after the 1% Unemployment Levy and 8% SIO (for nationals) has been deducted.

items.title: The SIO Cap
items.description: Calculate deductions only up to the BHD 4,000 monthly salary cap. Any amount above this is SIO-exempt.

items.title: Unemployment Levy
items.description: A flat 1% deduction applies to ALL employees (both local and expat) as part of the national welfare scheme.

items.title: Rounding Standards
items.description: Calculations should be maintained to three decimal places (fils) to match standard Bahraini banking and accounting practices.

items.title: Employer SIO (National)
items.description: Employers contribute 17% for Bahrainis, which includes the 3% work injury allowance.

items.title: Employer SIO (Expat)
items.description: Employers contribute a total of 3%, predominantly covering the work injury and healthcare components.

items.title: LMRA Monthly Fees
items.description: Include the BHD 5 monthly fee per expat employee (for the first 5 employees) in your total cost calculations.

items.title: First 3 Years
items.description: The calculator must accrue 15 days of the last basic salary per year for the first 36 months of service.

items.title: After 3 Years
items.description: The rate increases to 30 days (one full month) per year for every year thereafter.

items.title: Partial Year Gratuity
items.description: Employees are entitled to a pro-rated amount for any fraction of a year worked, provided they completed at least one year.

faqs.question: Does the calculator handle Hajj leave?
faqs.answer: Hajj leave is a one-time 21-day paid entitlement; it should be handled as a payout adjustment rather than a recurring cost.

faqs.question: Are transport allowances taxable?
faqs.answer: There is no income tax, but recurring transport allowances are included in the GOSI deduction base.

faqs.question: How accurate are the LMRA fee estimates?
faqs.answer: The calculator uses standard monthly fees; however, 'Tier 1' or 'Work Permit' renewal fees are one-time costs every 2 years.

items.title: CV/Resume

items.title: CR Renewal

items.title: VAT Submission

faqs.question: Can foreigners own 100% of a company?
faqs.answer: Yes, Bahrain allows 100% foreign ownership in the vast majority of commercial and industrial sectors.

faqs.question: Is a local partner required?
faqs.answer: Only in specific regulated sectors such as logistics, real estate, and certain retail activities.

faqs.question: How long does it take to open a bank account?
faqs.answer: Typically 2-4 weeks after the CR is issued, depending on the bank's KYC requirements.

faqs.question: What is the minimum wage for Bahrainis?
faqs.answer: BHD 300 for high school graduates, BHD 380 for diploma holders, and BHD 450 for degree holders.

faqs.question: Is it easy to terminate an employee?
faqs.answer: Termination without cause requires a 30-day notice and compensation of at least 2 days' pay per month of service (min 1 month total).

faqs.question: How do I verify a candidate's background?
faqs.answer: Professional agencies use local networking and Ministry verification for previous local employment history.

faqs.question: Are there zero-rated items for VAT?

faqs.question: When is the deadline for the annual audit?
faqs.answer: Audited accounts must be filed with the MOIC within 6 months of the end of the financial year.

faqs.question: Can I do my own bookkeeping?

faqs.question: Is the WPS mandatory for everyone?
faqs.answer: Yes, all employers in the private sector must transfer salaries through the Wage Protection System.

faqs.question: Do I need a local Data Protection Officer?

items.title: New Corporate Tax (CIT)

items.title: Regional VAT Alignment
items.description: Bahrain's VAT rate of 10% is aligned with regional neighbors while maintaining specific exemptions for social welfare.

items.title: Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax

items.title: Double Tax Treaties

items.title: Withholding Tax (WHT)

items.title: 100% Repatriation

items.title: Industrial Tax Holidays

items.title: No Capital Gains Tax
items.description: Bahrain generally does not tax capital gains, making it highly attractive for investment holding companies.

faqs.question: Does everyone pay the 15% Corporate Tax?
faqs.answer: No. Currently, it only applies to MNEs with global revenue exceeding EUR 750 million. Most SMEs remain at 0% CIT.

faqs.question: What is the VAT registration threshold?
faqs.answer: Mandatory once taxable supplies exceed BHD 37,500; voluntary registration is possible at BHD 18,750.

faqs.question: Are there taxes on real estate?
faqs.answer: There is a 2% registration fee (reduced to 1.7% if paid quickly) on the transfer of property ownership.
